To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) HIV-1 and/or immune-competent brain MP secretory products affect neurons in vitro and in vivo, (b) the effects on neurons are mediated by cell signaling events that include the MAPK pathway, and (c) the effects are electrophysiologically demonstrated by changes in neuronal function that include decreased excitability and/or synaptic plasticity.
HIV-1-inflicted brain MP products cause neuronal demise by altering neuronal function through the activation of signaling cascades and by inducing the release of toxic products.
MP secretory products cause neuronal dysfunction in vitro and in vivo, and that the mechanisms by which MP products affect neurons are via activation of cell signaling pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of neuronal injury and death during HAD, and we believe that our findings are relevant to other neurodegenerative diseases.
the role of brain MP in neuronal injury during HAD and the molecular mechanisms of how MP secretory activities affect neuronal physiology.
the effects of HIV-1 infection on the brain and the mechanisms of neurotoxicity.

the neuronal demise seen in HAD is caused, in part, by the MP secretory products.
the HIV-1-infested MP is a major player in the pathogenesis of HAD.
the neuronal demise in HAD is a result of a complex interplay of viral and cellular products from activated MP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV-1-inflected MP secretory products, which include viral and/or immune factors, can affect neuronal function leading to neuronal demise.
the MP factors are able to affect neurons by altering the levels of second messenger signaling molecules and/or by altering neuronal excitability.
the neuronal dysfunction in HAT, in part, is caused by MP factors which activate neuronal signaling pathways, resulting in neuronal cell death.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MP secretory products are capable of altering neuronal physiology, and that such alterations may lead to neuronal demise in HAD.
MP secretory products, in concert with viral proteins, can affect neuronal physiology leading, in the long run, to cellular demise.
the neuronal damage in HAD is not caused by a single factor but rather by a complex interplay among multiple viral and immune products from brain MP.
